 Hyderabad Sankranti ticket scramble begins early in Hyderabad 
 Train waiting lists touch 200, forcing people to turn to costly private buses & seek special services to travel home Regular trains such as Garib Rath, Godavari, Janmabhoomi and Visakha Express have already moved to the ‘regret’ status, while premium services, including Duronto and Vande Bharat Express, are showing waiting lists of nearly 200 in several cases. File Photo. Siddhardha Gattimi Updated on :  16 Nov 2026, 3:38 am 2 min read 
 Copied 
 HYDERABAD: With Sankranti two months away, passengers travelling from Hyderabad to major destinations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are already struggling to secure train tickets. Several popular services are showing no availability on peak travel dates between January 8 and 15. 
 Regular trains such as Garib Rath, Godavari, Janmabhoomi and Visakha Express have already moved to the ‘regret’ status, while premium services, including Duronto and Vande Bharat Express, are showing waiting lists of nearly 200 in several cases.
 With advance reservations opening 60 days before the date of journey, passengers planning to visit their native places have been closely monitoring the booking portal, trying to secure confirmed berths as soon as reservations begin. While some have managed to book tickets, many others are now exploring private buses and other alternatives. Passengers are also hoping that the South Central Railway will announce special trains to handle the festival rush.
 Speaking to TNIE, R Nava Teja, a software employee, said he had planned to travel to his native place, Visakhapatnam, on January 9, as the festival coincides with a long weekend. “The bookings were to open at 8 am and I was ready with my laptop. The website took nearly two minutes to load and, by the time I reached the payment stage, the Garib Rath was showing a waiting list of 200. When I checked other trains, they had already moved to the regret status,” he said.
 As train berths become increasingly difficult to find, several passengers have started turning to private buses despite the steep fares. Sleeper tickets are currently priced at more than Rs 2,500, while seater tickets cost upwards of Rs 1,700. Passengers are also tracking fare fluctuations, hoping prices will drop before they book. Meanwhile, tickets on TGSRTC and APSRTC services are also filling up fast.
 However, booking a private bus ticket in advance does not always guarantee a hassle-free journey. K Uday Kiran, another software employee in Hyderabad, said he had faced last-minute cancellations despite booking tickets early to avoid festival-time fare hikes.
 With demand expected to rise further as the festival approaches, passengers are looking to the Railways to introduce additional services. Special trains to major destinations in Andhra Pradesh, particularly Visakhapatnam, Rajamahendravaram and Vijayawada, are among their key demands, as regular services are already witnessing heavy bookings.
 Air travel is another option, though at a higher cost. Flight fares from Hyderabad to Visakhapatnam are currently starting at around Rs 5,000, while tickets to Vijayawada are available from around Rs 2,800.
